राजधानी में शनिवार सुबह से तेज धूप निकली हुई है। धूप के चलते दिन में गर्मी का असर बढ़ा है। मौसम विभाग के अनुसार आने वाले समय में छुटपुट बारिश के आसार बने रहेंगे। हालांकि बारिश के बावजूद तापमान में बढ़ोतरी होने की संभावना है। मौसम में उतार-चढ़ाव के चलते लोगों को उमस और गर्मी का सामना करना पड़ सकता है। राजधानी में सुबह से ही आसमान साफ रहा और धूप तेज होने के कारण सड़कों पर गर्मी का असर नजर आया। मौसम विभाग ने स्थानीय स्तर पर कहीं-कहीं हल्की बारिश की संभावना जताई है।

उत्तर में धूप खिली हुई है और तापमान में तेजी से वृद्धि हो रही है, जबकि मध्य क्षेत्र में मूसलाधार बारिश हो रही है।
एसकेडीएस - उत्तरी वियतनाम में भीषण गर्मी पड़ रही है और तापमान अधिकतम 33 डिग्री सेल्सियस तक पहुंच गया है, जबकि मध्य वियतनाम के कई क्षेत्रों में भारी बारिश हो रही है और व्यापक बाढ़ की चेतावनी जारी की गई है।
Báo Sức khỏe và Đời sống•11/09/2026
राष्ट्रीय मौसम विज्ञान एवं जल विज्ञान पूर्वानुमान केंद्र के अनुसार, उत्तरी वियतनाम में स्थिर ठंडी हवा का प्रभाव बना हुआ है, जो धीरे-धीरे कमजोर हो जाएगा। 12 सितंबर को, क्षेत्र में मौसम शुष्क रहेगा, धूप खिली रहेगी और तापमान में मामूली वृद्धि होगी, जो अधिकतम 31-33 डिग्री सेल्सियस तक पहुंच जाएगा।
विशेष रूप से 12 सितंबर को हनोई में छिटपुट बारिश होगी, दोपहर में बादल छंटेंगे और आसमान साफ रहेगा; उत्तर-पूर्वी हवाएं 2-3 स्तर की होंगी। अधिकतम तापमान 31-33 डिग्री सेल्सियस के बीच रहेगा और रात का न्यूनतम तापमान 22-25 डिग्री सेल्सियस के आसपास रहेगा।
कल रात और आज सुबह (12 सितंबर) क्वांग त्रि प्रांत के दक्षिण से क्वांग न्गाई तक और जिया लाई से डाक लक तक के पूर्वी प्रांतों में मध्यम से भारी बारिश और गरज के साथ बौछारें पड़ीं, कुछ इलाकों में तो बहुत भारी बारिश हुई। 11 सितंबर की शाम 7 बजे से 12 सितंबर की सुबह 3 बजे तक कुछ स्थानों पर बारिश की मात्रा 150 मिमी से अधिक रही, जैसे कि ताम लान्ह ( दा नांग ) में 195.4 मिमी और त्रा थान्ह (क्वांग न्गाई) में 159.2 मिमी।
12 सितंबर की सुबह से लेकर 12 सितंबर की रात तक, हा तिन्ह से लेकर क्वांग त्रि प्रांत के उत्तरी भाग तक के क्षेत्र में मध्यम से भारी बारिश और गरज के साथ बौछारें पड़ीं, जिसमें आमतौर पर 40-80 मिमी बारिश हुई, जबकि कुछ क्षेत्रों में 150 मिमी से अधिक बहुत भारी बारिश हुई; क्वांग त्रि प्रांत के दक्षिणी भाग से लेकर क्वांग न्गाई तक के क्षेत्र में भारी से बहुत भारी बारिश और गरज के साथ बौछारें पड़ीं, जिसमें आमतौर पर 80-150 मिमी बारिश हुई, जबकि कुछ क्षेत्रों में 250 मिमी से अधिक बारिश हुई।
13 सितंबर को, दिन और रात दोनों समय, दक्षिणी न्घे आन प्रांत से दा नांग शहर तक के क्षेत्र में भारी से बहुत भारी बारिश और गरज के साथ तूफान आया। बारिश की मात्रा आम तौर पर 80-180 मिमी के बीच रही, और कुछ इलाकों में 300 मिमी से अधिक भी दर्ज की गई। थान्ह होआ से उत्तरी न्घे आन प्रांत और पूर्वी क्वांग न्गाई प्रांत तक के क्षेत्र में मध्यम से भारी बारिश और गरज के साथ तूफान आया। बारिश की मात्रा आम तौर पर 30-70 मिमी के बीच रही, और कुछ इलाकों में 120 मिमी से अधिक भी दर्ज की गई। भारी बारिश (>100 मिमी/3 घंटे) के खतरे के संबंध में चेतावनी जारी की गई है।
इसके अतिरिक्त, 12 सितंबर को दिन और रात दोनों समय, जिया लाई से लाम डोंग तक के प्रांतों के पूर्वी क्षेत्रों, मध्य उच्चभूमि और दक्षिणी क्षेत्र में 20-40 मिमी तक की बारिश, मध्यम बारिश और छिटपुट गरज के साथ बौछारें पड़ेंगी, और कुछ स्थानों पर 80 मिमी से अधिक भारी बारिश भी हो सकती है। गरज के साथ बौछारों के दौरान बवंडर, बिजली, ओले और तेज हवा के झोंके चलने की संभावना है।
14 सितंबर को, दिन और रात दोनों समय, उत्तरी वियतनाम के मध्य और निचले इलाकों और सोन ला, तुयेन क्वांग और लाओ काई प्रांतों के दक्षिणी भागों में मध्यम से भारी बारिश और गरज के साथ बौछारें पड़ेंगी। बारिश की मात्रा आमतौर पर 30-60 मिमी के बीच रहेगी और कुछ स्थानों पर 100 मिमी से अधिक भी हो सकती है। थान्ह होआ से क्वांग त्रि तक के क्षेत्र में भारी से बहुत भारी बारिश और गरज के साथ बौछारें पड़ेंगी। बारिश की मात्रा आमतौर पर 70-150 मिमी के बीच रहेगी और कुछ स्थानों पर 250 मिमी से अधिक भी हो सकती है। इन क्षेत्रों में भारी बारिश 16 सितंबर की सुबह तक जारी रहने की संभावना है। भारी बारिश के कारण प्राकृतिक आपदा का खतरा स्तर 1 है।
12 सितंबर को देशभर के सभी क्षेत्रों के लिए मौसम का पूर्वानुमान:
आपको यह भी पसंद आ सकता है
हनोई शहर
न्यूनतम तापमान 23-26 डिग्री; अधिकतम तापमान 31-33 डिग्री। दिन में बादल छाए रहेंगे, धूप निकलेगी, रात में बारिश नहीं होगी। उत्तर-पूर्वी हवा, गति 2-3।
उत्तर-पश्चिमी वियतनाम
न्यूनतम तापमान 22-25 डिग्री सेल्सियस रहेगा, कुछ क्षेत्रों में 21 डिग्री से नीचे भी जा सकता है; अधिकतम तापमान 29-32 डिग्री सेल्सियस रहेगा, कुछ क्षेत्रों में 32 डिग्री से ऊपर भी जा सकता है। दिन में बादल छाए रहेंगे और धूप निकलेगी, रात में छिटपुट बारिश और गरज के साथ तूफान आने की संभावना है। हवा हल्की चलेगी।
पूर्वोत्तर वियतनाम
न्यूनतम तापमान 23-26 डिग्री सेल्सियस, पहाड़ी क्षेत्रों में 22 डिग्री सेल्सियस से नीचे; अधिकतम तापमान 30-33 डिग्री सेल्सियस। दिन में बादल छाए रहेंगे, धूप निकलेगी, रात में छिटपुट बारिश और गरज के साथ तूफान आएगा। उत्तर-पूर्वी हवा, गति 2-3।
थान्ह होआ से ह्यू
न्यूनतम तापमान 22-25 डिग्री सेल्सियस; अधिकतम 27-30 डिग्री सेल्सियस। उत्तर (थान्ह होआ और न्घे आन) में बादल छाए रहेंगे और छिटपुट बारिश और गरज के साथ तूफान आने की संभावना है; दक्षिण में मध्यम से भारी बारिश और छिटपुट गरज के साथ तूफान आने की संभावना है, कुछ क्षेत्रों में बहुत भारी बारिश हो सकती है। उत्तर से उत्तर-पश्चिम की ओर हवा चलेगी, जिसकी तीव्रता 2-3 ब्यूफोर्ट स्केल होगी। गरज के साथ तूफान के दौरान बवंडर, बिजली गिरने और तेज हवा के झोंके आने की संभावना है।
दक्षिण मध्य तट
न्यूनतम तापमान 23-26 डिग्री सेल्सियस; अधिकतम तापमान उत्तर में 27-30 डिग्री सेल्सियस और दक्षिण में 30-32 डिग्री सेल्सियस रहेगा। उत्तर में बादल छाए रहेंगे, मध्यम से भारी बारिश और छिटपुट गरज के साथ बौछारें पड़ेंगी, और कुछ क्षेत्रों में बहुत भारी बारिश होगी; दक्षिण में बारिश, मध्यम बारिश और छिटपुट गरज के साथ बौछारें पड़ेंगी, और कुछ क्षेत्रों में भारी बारिश होगी। दक्षिण-पश्चिम दिशा से 2-3 ब्यूफोर्ट की गति से हवाएं चलेंगी। गरज के साथ बौछारों के दौरान बवंडर, बिजली गिरने और तेज हवा के झोंके आने की संभावना है।
मध्य उच्चभूमि
आपको यह भी पसंद आ सकता है
न्यूनतम तापमान 19-22 डिग्री; अधिकतम 26-29 डिग्री। बादल छाए रहेंगे, हल्की बारिश और छिटपुट गरज के साथ बौछारें पड़ेंगी, कुछ क्षेत्रों में भारी बारिश हो सकती है। दक्षिण-पश्चिम दिशा से 2-3 की गति से हवा चलेगी। गरज के साथ बौछारों के दौरान बवंडर, बिजली गिरने और तेज हवा के झोंके आने की संभावना है।
दक्षिणी वियतनाम
न्यूनतम तापमान 23-26 डिग्री सेल्सियस; अधिकतम तापमान 29-32 डिग्री सेल्सियस। बादल छाए रहेंगे, हल्की बारिश और छिटपुट गरज के साथ बौछारें पड़ेंगी, कुछ क्षेत्रों में भारी बारिश हो सकती है। दक्षिण-पश्चिम दिशा से 2-3 तीव्रता की हवा चलेगी। गरज के साथ बौछारों के दौरान बवंडर, बिजली गिरने और तेज हवा के झोंके आने की संभावना है।
हो ची मिन्ह सिटी

articles.full_text:
At least 23 prisoners have died in Tunisia in recent weeks due to extreme heat, according to rights advocates, who have long condemned harsh detention conditions made worse by overcrowding.
Authorities have yet to release figures for prison deaths this summer, with an official saying no death could be attributed to heat without confirmation from forensic doctors.
Yet the Tunisian League for Human Rights (LTDH) documented 23 deaths based on information from doctors, lawyers and relatives of prisoners who died in jail from the heat, its president Bassem Trifi told AFP.
Tunisia has suffered high temperatures in recent weeks, with residents struggling with long power outages and water cuts.
Among the dead detainees was businessman Lazhar Sta, his daughter said. Another was a 24-year-old student, according to local media.
A Lebanese businessman also died in a Tunisian prison, said Trifi. A Lebanese judicial source told AFP that his father had informed Lebanese authorities of his death a week earlier.
"Conditions are already inhumane under normal circumstances, but with the heatwave and temperatures that sometimes exceed 45C in overcrowded cells, the situation becomes a threat to prisoners' lives," Trifi said.
Tunisian prisons have long faced criticism over chronic overcrowding and poor detention conditions.
Rights groups have said cells are overcrowded, with inadequate ventilation and a limited access to water -- accusations the prison administration has denied.
The World Organisation Against Torture (OMCT) said this week it was "concerned about the deterioration of detention conditions and the increase in deaths in prisons".
The group also called for "transparent" and "independent" investigations amid what it said was a lack of official data around the deaths.
Relatives of detainees had already raised concerns about detention conditions as temperatures rose over the summer.
Warnings from relatives of prominent jailed critics of President Kais Saied were widely circulated on social media.
The figures include Ennahdha party leader Rached Ghannouchi, 85, whose lawyers in July said his health was "critical" after reports that he fainted and suffered severe exhaustion behind bars.
Also among them is 82-year-old activist Ahmed Nejib Chebbi, whose daughter also expressed concern over the conditions in which he and others were detained.
"I will not wait for my father and uncle to die in prison," Haifa Chebbi, a lawyer, said.
Her uncle Issam Chebbi is also imprisoned over charges rights groups have denounced as politically motivated.
"I will not remain silent. Free the detainees," she wrote on social media.
Prison authorities in July said all detainees were receiving "medical care according to regulations" and that "all necessary measures" were taken in response to the heat.
Dozens of political figures, journalists and businessmen, among others, have been detained since Saied staged a sweeping power grab in 2021.
The OMCT called on Tunisian authorities to take "the necessary measures to protect the life" of detainees and to allow rights groups to conduct prison visits.
The LTDH had said it was banned from visiting prisons since November 2025.
In recent days, concerns have grown over the health of investigative journalist Mohamed Yousfi.
Yousfi was arrested last week while he was set to discuss water shortages on a radio show. He later underwent surgery for appendicitis.
The National Syndicate of Tunisian Journalists (SNJT) said members of his defence had to leave an interrogation to get him medication as Yousfi was "screaming loudly from pain".
And the daughter of jailed independent journalist Zied El Heni, also a Saied critic, expressed fears for her father.
"Every time I visit my father, I am afraid they will tell me he died," Aram El Heni said in a widely shared video on Facebook.
"Every time I leave the prison, I tell myself it may be the last time I see him."

Battling heatwave havoc, giant veg growers prepare for judgement
Across allotments and deep in the heart of gardens, excitement is building ahead of a big date in the calendar - the Canna UK National Giant Vegetables Championship, later this month.
For the many who spend months tending their plants to get their vegetables as big as possible, the time for judging is nigh, with the show starting on 25 September.
Take for instance Neil Hands - talk to him about why he gave up coaching a children's football team to take on his own allotment and that is when he really lights up.
Eighteen years into his vegetable-growing journey, he said his proudest moment was winning a Guinness World Record four years in a row, for the biggest red cabbage.
"I used to watch Alan Titchmarsh on Gardeners' World and that was it," he smiled.
"I took an allotment on and never looked back."
After his world records, Hands' hopes are high of another winning time for his red cabbage, at the championship in Malvern, Worcestershire.
While he lives in Walsall, he says he is part of a community of growers, spanning the country.
"The camaraderie is wicked. Everyone is so helpful and anyone can do it," he grinned.
"You just need to keep checking on your veg, get tips, watch tutorials on YouTube and my biggest tip is make sure you get the proper seeds."
The show is widely known as one of the UK's biggest harvest‑season celebrations, drawing thousands of visitors to the Three Counties Showground each September.
Growers enter supersized pumpkins, marrows, cabbages and more - often breaking world records each year.
Last year, records fell for the world's longest radish and heaviest celeriac, as well as UK and EU records for giant tomatoes.
More than 100 competitors are expected to take part, with rivalry described as fierce..
Growers present enormous, often record‑breaking vegetables ranging from celery and leeks to parsnips and cabbages.
Kate Dufton, who manages the event, said the stereotype of it only being men in their allotments was wrong - women have long been central to the show.
"From award-winning growers and floral artists to bakers, makers, gardeners and entrepreneurs, women have long played a vital role in shaping the rich traditions and vibrant atmosphere of Malvern Autumn Show," she said.
"Whether cultivating spectacular blooms, creating beautiful handmade products, demonstrating culinary skills or championing sustainable growing, women continue to be at the heart of the harvest season."
For some growers, the focus is all on the soil - others look at their manure, whether chicken or horse.
For Derek Hulme, it is Tender Loving Care - TLC - which is the order of the day when it comes to his approach.
The 65-year-old, from Stoke-on-Trent, told the BBC: "It all comes down to the weather conditions. You need some TLC and a lot of different variants to succeed. There's a lot to it.
"But the weather is a massive part. A lot of growers giant pumpkin and marrow growers have been devastated because their vegetables have split.
"The conditions have been so dry, we're watering more. But then the vegetables soak up more than it can actually cope with and then they split wide open."
The heatwaves this year have played havoc with the competitors, with Hands adding "it's been terrible".
"It's too hot for my cabbages this year, they need it to be cooler. I've just been watering and watering," he admitted, saying everyone was panicking.
'It's very strange'
The love of growing vegetables can start at a young age - for Hulme, it sprouted when he was a teenage barrow boy on the market in his home city, carrying produce for stallholders and customers.
The hobby side began when he started finessing things at his allotment and grew from there.
"As soon as I saw the giant veg in Malvern all those years ago - it was hook line and sinker," he smiled.
"It's a very strange thing to do, giant vegetable growing."
"It isn't like normal vegetables. If you lose one, you lose your hard work."
Hulme is taking his huge pumpkin - which he estimates already weighs more than 500lb (226kg), comparable to a tractor tyre - to the show this year.
"My best tip, if you want to get into growing, is get the right seed. It's got to come from a reputable grower," he added.

Temperatures are set to climb across the UK this weekend, reaching summerlike levels in some places.
It will feel warm and muggy - especially where there are sunny spells - although heavy rain also features in the forecast.
The warmth will persist into Monday in many areas but nowhere is expected to reach heatwave criteria and cooler conditions are due to return by midweek.
Computer weather models paint a very mixed picture for the second half of September but, while there are likely to be some warm spells, there are currently no definitive signs of a heatwave.
How warm will it get this weekend?
Outbreaks of rain will spread southwards during Saturday, clearing from Scotland and Northern Ireland but continuing into the afternoon across parts of northern England, Wales and the Midlands.
Some of the rain could be heavy with a chance of thunder and lightning and will be accompanied by brisk south-westerly winds.
Southern parts of England should stay largely dry with sunny intervals and it will feel particularly warm and humid with temperatures climbing into the mid-20s Celsius - several degrees above the September average.
On Sunday, rain may linger for a while in southern England but should clear to leave a dry afternoon for much of the UK with sunny spells and light winds.
Temperatures may drop slightly in the northern half of the country but rise a little further south. Parts of Wales, the Midlands and southern England could reach 23-25C.
Monday could be even warmer with highs of 22-26C across much of England and Wales, and 20C likely in parts of Scotland and Northern Ireland.
However, while this will undoubtedly feel warm, it will remain below the criteria for a heatwave.
This would require three consecutive days of temperatures above a threshold which varies from 25C in Scotland and Northern Ireland to 28C in the London area.
Is there hot weather in the long-range forecast?
Computer models currently suggest unsettled weather will continue over the next week or so.
The jet stream is expected to bring areas of low pressure across the UK - meaning spells of rain and, potentially, some rather blustery winds.
The prospect of wet weather will be welcome for the large swathes of England and Wales that remain in drought.
Later in the month, areas of high pressure may have more influence on the weather which would mean longer dry interludes and the chance of above-average daytime temperatures.
While long-range forecasting is fraught with uncertainty and details are subject to change, there is currently nothing to indicate that a heatwave is on the cards.
Indeed, as autumn advances and the nights become longer, high pressure overhead could lead to some rather chilly mornings.
You can keep an eye on the temperatures where you are by checking BBC Weather online and the app.

Summer-like temperatures are set to return early next week following a rainy start to September, with temperatures set to soar to 25C.
The Met office says warm weather and sunny spells are set to make a comeback this weekend, although heavy rain also features in the forecast.
It’s set to stay warm until Monday when temperatures could reach mid 20C in the south of England. But later in the week cooler condition are predicted to return.
On Saturday, wet weather is expected to move towards the south, with rain clearing in Scotland and Northern Ireland but continuing into the afternoon in northern England, Wales and the Midlands.
However, southern parts of England are forecast to stay mostly dry with sunny spells and temperatures climbing to 24C in London and 20C in Plymouth.

Monday could be even warmer, with highs of 25C expected in London and 22C in Manchester and Cardiff. It will also likely reach 20C in parts of Scotland.
These temperatures are not quite warm enough to meet the criteria for a heatwave, which needs at least three consecutive days of temperatures above about 28C in the London area or 25C in Scotland.
It comes after the Met Office confirmed the UK had experienced its hottest summer since records began nearly 150 years ago.
Five heatwaves between May and August have left the majority of the country in drought and have sparked wildfires and travel disruption.
The UK recorded a mean average temperature across June, July and August of 16.5C, beating the previous seasonal high of 16.1C set last year, the Met Office said.
The highest temperature recorded this summer was on 13 August at Kew Gardens, when the mercury hit 38.1C.
Changeable conditions with occasional rain or showers arriving from the North Atlantic, are set to be frequent in northern and western parts of the UK until the end of September, according to the Met Office.
But there will also be some dry and more settled periods in the south.
Towards the end of September high pressure may become more dominant bringing more settled conditions, with warmer daytime temperatures and cooler nights.

Outbreaks of rain in the north and strong winds. Rain could be heavy at times across northern England, Wales and the Midlands. Drier in the south and rather breezy, with some warm sunny spells.

Winds gradually easing overnight as rain moves further south. Staying cloudy and humid in the south, but fresher with clearer spells in the north.

Cloud and outbreaks of rain linger in the south on Sunday, but rain gradually easing. Still warm and humid here. Drier, brighter and fresher in the north with sunny spells.

Changeable over the next few days with spells of rain and showers, interspersed with some drier and brighter weather. Warm at first, but turning fresher from Tuesday. Breezy at times.

Environment: light winds reduce CO₂ uptake in the Mediterranean
This is the finding of a study by researchers at ENEA, which collects continuous data on the exchange of carbon dioxide between the atmosphere and the sea
Light winds reduce CO₂ absorption in the Mediterranean. Specifically, in early 2023, the central Mediterranean absorbed 30 per cent less carbon dioxide than in the same period the previous year, coinciding with light winds and an intense marine heatwave. This is one of the key findings of a study carried out by researchers at ENEA and published in the *Journal of Geophysical Research: Oceans*, which, for the first time, compiles continuous data on carbon dioxide exchanges between the atmosphere and the sea in this part of the Mediterranean.
The impact of the heatwave
According to Alcide di Sarra, a researcher at ENEA’s Laboratory for Air Quality Modelling and Measurements and Climate Observations, the exceptional heatwave that occurred ‘most likely also had a significant impact on CO₂ exchange between the atmosphere and the ocean, resulting in a significant release from the ocean into the atmosphere’. ‘The data collected at the Lampedusa Oceanographic Observatory during the exceptional marine heatwave of summer 2026 – adds di Sarra, who, together with Damiano Sferlazzo, is in charge of the Lampedusa Oceanographic Observatory – show temperature readings that exceeded 31°C at a depth of 1 metre, and 30°C at depths of 5 and 18 metres. Such high values, sustained over such an extended period, have never been observed since records began.”
Measurements between 2021 and 2023
At the heart of the study are measurements taken between 2021 and 2023 in the central Mediterranean, which, as di Sarra points out, ‘acts as a large carbon dioxide reservoir, absorbing CO₂ from the atmosphere in winter and releasing it during the summer’. Hence the sea’s role in removing carbon dioxide. “The data collected are the first to show that, on an annual basis, this region of the Mediterranean helps to remove CO₂ from the atmosphere,” he adds. ‘Between May 2022 and April 2023, however, we observed a marked reduction in CO₂ exchange between the atmosphere and the sea, coinciding with an intense and prolonged marine heatwave,’ he adds.
Temperatures have risen
The study also reveals that, as early as 2022, the surface temperature of the Mediterranean Sea was ‘significantly higher than the average values for the period 1991–2020, due to an intense and persistent marine heatwave, which lasted from May 2022 to April 2023’. On average, across the entire basin, the increase reached around 1.5–2 °C, whilst in the central Mediterranean even higher peaks were recorded, up to 4 °C above the seasonal average. During the same period, the researchers observed ‘a marked reduction in the frequency of strong winds, with 42 daily average wind speeds exceeding 8 m/s, compared with the 71 recorded in the previous year’. Conversely, ‘the number of days characterised by light winds increased, with 47 days on which the average daily wind speed was below 5 m/s, compared with just 26 days in the previous year’. These conditions, the researchers emphasise, ‘have helped to sustain the marine heatwave in the study area, the central Mediterranean’.
The basis for new observations
Not a final result, but a starting point for further research. “Thanks to over a year and a half of continuous monitoring, we have been able to measure the impact of this extreme weather event on the marine carbon cycle,” concludes di Sarra. ‘These data form the basis for building a long-term set of observations, which will help us better understand the evolution of these phenomena in a climate hotspot such as the Mediterranean, which is particularly sensitive to climate change and increasingly characterised by extreme events such as Mediterranean hurricanes – known as medicane – and marine heatwaves,’.

Heavy rain forecast across Saurashtra
Rainy conditions are likely to continue on September 14. Extremely heavy rain is forecast at isolated places in Dang, Navsari and Valsad in South Gujarat, while Bharuch, Surat and Tapi may receive heavy rain. Several districts of Saurashtra are also likely to witness heavy rainfall.
Heavy rain likely in Saurashtra and South Gujarat on September 15
On September 15, heavy rain is likely in Valsad, Daman and Dadra and Nagar Haveli. Heavy rain has also been forecast in Jamnagar, Porbandar, Junagadh, Dwarka and Gir Somnath in Saurashtra.
Ahmedabad likely to remain cloudy
Ahmedabad is likely to remain generally cloudy today, September 12, with light rain possible. The city recorded a maximum temperature of 35.5°C and a minimum of 24.5°C. Ahmedabad has received 595.7 mm of rainfall so far this season, which is 97.3 mm below normal.

THIRUVANANTHAPURAM: The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has predcited the possibility of rain in Kerala over the next three days. A yellow alert has been issued in several districts. A yellow alert has been declared in Pathanamthitta, Idukki, and Palakkad on Monday; Malappuram, Kozhikode, and Wayanad on Tuesday; and Idukki, Kozhikode, Wayanad, and Kannur on Wednesday.
Isolated instances of heavy rainfall have been predicted. Heavy rain refers to rainfall of 64.5 mm to 115.5 mm within 24 hours.
Alert issued
Lightning is dangerous. It can cause serious damage to human and animal lives, electrical and communication networks, and household appliances connected to electrical conductors. Therefore, the public is advised to take the following precautions as soon as dark clouds begin to appear. Since lightning may not always be visible, these precautions should not be ignored.
As soon as the first signs of lightning are noticed, move immediately to a safe building. Staying in open areas increases the risk of being struck by lightning.
When strong winds and lightning are expected, keep doors and windows closed. Do not stand near doors or windows. Stay inside the building and try to avoid touching walls or floors as much as possible.
Disconnect electrical appliances from the power supply. Avoid being near electrical equipment during thunderstorms.
Avoid using landline telephones during lightning. Using mobile phones is safe.
If the sky is cloudy, avoid playing or spending time in open areas or on terraces, including children.
Do not stand under trees during thunderstorms. Do not park vehicles under trees either.
During lightning, remain inside your vehicle and do not extend your hands or feet outside. You are relatively safe inside a vehicle. Avoid travelling on bicycles, motorcycles, tractors, and similar vehicles during thunderstorms. Seek shelter in a safe building and remain there until the lightning has stopped.
When rain clouds appear, do not go to the terrace or courtyard to collect clothes while lightning is occurring.
Secure objects that could be blown away or knocked down by strong winds.
Avoid bathing during thunderstorms. Also avoid collecting water from taps, as electricity caused by lightning may travel through plumbing.
Do not enter water bodies to fish or bathe during thunderstorms. As soon as dark clouds begin to appear, stop activities such as fishing and boating and try to reach the nearest shore immediately. Do not stand on the deck of a boat during lightning. Stop activities such as casting fishing lines or throwing nets during thunderstorms.
Avoid flying kites.

Javed Rana reviews development, flood relief measures in Surankote
Excelsior Correspondent SURANKOTE, Sept 11: The Minister for Jal Shakti, Forest, Ecology & Environment and Tribal Affairs Javed Rana today chaired a comprehensive review meeting of development works and post-flood relief and restoration measures. The meeting was attended by MLA...
Excelsior Correspondent
SURANKOTE, Sept 11: The Minister for Jal Shakti, Forest, Ecology & Environment and Tribal Affairs Javed Rana today chaired a comprehensive review meeting of development works and post-flood relief and restoration measures.
The meeting was attended by MLA Surankote, Chowdhary Akram, SDM Surankote Farooq Khan, and senior officers and Heads of Departments from Jal Shakti, Rural Development Department (RDD), PWD, Irrigation & Flood Control, PDD, Agriculture, Horticulture and other allied departments.
At the outset, the MLA highlighted various key issues and developmental concerns pertaining to Surankote Assembly Constituency and sought timely intervention for their resolution.
SDM Surankote Farooq Khan made a detailed presentation on the damages caused by the recent floods and cloudbursts, the corrective and restoration measures undertaken by the administration so far, and the future course of action.
The HoDs of various departments also presented the status of works undertaken, ongoing restoration activities, proposed works and future plans in their respective sectors. The meeting reviewed the progress of restoration and rehabilitation works and identified key areas requiring immediate attention.
Minister directed the Jal Shakti Department to prepare and submit a detailed DPR for strengthening and improving the water supply system of Surankote town. He also directed the department to formulate detailed proposals for lift irrigation schemes, particularly in areas where irrigation kuls have been damaged due to the recent floods, resulting in disruption of agricultural activities, especially paddy cultivation.
The Minister directed the Forest Department to further intensify its efforts and ensure visible progress on the ground. He also impressed upon all departments to adopt a people-centric approach, remain accessible and responsive to public grievances, and ensure timely delivery of services.
Emphasising the need for coordinated and result-oriented functioning, the Minister called upon all officers and officials to work with greater zeal, enthusiasm and dedication and remain committed to the welfare and betterment of the people.
He also decided to hold regular public meetings at Surankote to directly interact with the people, assess their grievances and ensure timely redressal of issues pertaining to various departments.
The meeting concluded with directions for close inter-departmental coordination, expeditious execution of restoration and developmental works, and continuous monitoring of progress to ensure tangible benefits for the people of Surankote.
